body:
resolves: #22297 

## Todo:

### charwise range parsing:

- [x] Support backtick ranges pass column info to the command
  ```
  :`<,`>foo
  :`a,`bfoo
  ```
- [x] Column info is available as `<col1> , <col2>` (like :help <line1>)
  - For user-defined command, `:command -addr=lines`
- [x] Support `x.y` ranges pass column info to the command
  ```
  :1.2,2.2 foo
  ```
- [x] Update nvim_parse_cmd() , nvim_cmd()
- [ ] Update docs: :help :range
- [ ] Document the rest.

### Add support charwise range to Ex commands:

- [x] ! — Filter range through shell command (do_filter)
- [x] & — Repeat last substitution
- [x] ~ — Repeat last substitution with search pattern
- [x] :append (:a) — Append text after position (col2)
- [x] :change (:c) — Change character range (col1..col2)
- [x] :copy (:co, :t) — Copy character range to destination position (dest_col)
- [x] :delete (:d) — Delete character range (col1..col2)
- [x] :global (:g) — Execute command on lines matching pattern, preserving character-wise mode
- [x] :insert (:i) — Insert text before position (col2)
- [x] :iput — Put register contents before position (col2)
- [x] :move (:m) — Move character range to destination position (dest_col)
- [x] :put — Put register contents after position (col2)
- [x] :read (:r) — Read file/command output at position (col2)
- [x] :smagic — Substitute with 'magic' pattern
- [x] :snomagic — Substitute with 'nomagic' pattern
- [x] :substitute (:s) — Substitute pattern within character range (col1..col2)
- [x] :vglobal (:v) — Execute command on lines not matching pattern, preserving character-wise mode
- [x] :write (:w) — Write character range (col1..col2) to file
- [x] :yank (:y) — Yank character range (col1..col2)
- [x] < — Shift text left within character-wise range
- [x] = — Format code within character-wise range
- [x] > — Shift text right within character-wise range
- [x] :center — Center text within character-wise column boundaries
- [x] :join (:j) — Join lines starting from col1 through col2
- [x] :left — Left-align text within character-wise column boundaries
- [x] :luado — Execute Lua code over line slices within character-wise range
- [ ] :perldo — Execute Perl code over line slices within character-wise range
- [ ] :pydo / :py3do / :pyxdo — Execute Python code over line slices within character-wise range
- [x] :retab — Retab spaces/tabs within character-wise bounds (col1..col2)
- [x] :right — Right-align text within character-wise column boundaries
- [ ] :rubydo — Execute Ruby code over line slices within character-wise range
- [x] :sort — Sort lines or substrings within character-wise bounds
- [x] :uniq — Remove duplicate lines or substrings within character-wise bounds

(todo's extracted from https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/22297#issuecomment-1442415792)

comment_data.body:
Seems like this could have a "lifetime" issue. `eap->do_ecmd_cmd` may get freed and the new `ea.cmd` might not expect that?

`XFREE_CLEAR` may be useful.

Might be worth exploring whether `write_output` can just collect the output and pass it to an Ex command (or Lua, or some internal function) to do the actual replacement. That could save a lot of code here.

Is there any reason we need to support both "lines" and "charwise" internally? Could a "linewise" (external) command (e.g. `:'<,'>foo`) just be converted to charwise (internally)? Then that might avoid a lot of conditional checks everywhere?
Good idea, I will look into it.

This was also my initial idea, because it feels like there are only two different modes `blockwise` and `charwise`, while `linewise` just being charwise with col1=0 and col2=ml_get_pos_len(line2)+1 (I think also it's better to be inclusive by default internally).

I don't remember what exactly was the issue that let me change my mind there, if this was just to many places to change or some incosistencies in current implementation, because many functions don't consider columns and the other that do have different handling for charwise and linewise behavior.

Regardless I still think that would be better for the future to always act in line1:col1,line2:col2 ranges, it feels more natural and easier to understand (at least for me :D).

TLDR: I give it another shot and ether come with a proper list of `why not` or with an bigger PR to review :).

@justinmk I thaught about the exact implementation about what you suggesting, do you actually mean the parsed command table should have only 'char' in the 'addr' field? Because there are functions that already accept an parsed command table and they would break if we only provide 'char', the other way around could also break some clients and may be confusing if we have 'addr' always set to 'line' and provide col values that not represent whole line selections. Just trying to understand which implementation you suggesting.

> the other way around could also break some clients

I only meant internally, in the C code. When you say "clients" that makes me think of external consumers.

By "clients" I mean anyone who uses `vim.api.nvim_parse_cmd` and `vim.api.nvim_cmd`, do we wan't there to have `addr=char` or do we want to handle that with `addr=line` and e.g. `range = { 1, 2, 3, 4 }` for charwise selections. What do you think?
My suggestion here was only about the internal C code. How we expose things in `nvim_cmd` is not bound to that.
Ok than this was a misunderstanding from my site, thanks for clarifying

this and `ml_replace_range_in_line` are *hopefully* already covered by `nvim_buf_set_text` ?  and `ml_append_pos` I assume may be covered by `nvim_put` .

it's true that those are "API" functions, so maybe they're awkward to use internally. but then, I would suggest extracting the common bits out into a shared memline concept. the logic is extremely non-trivial and we want to get it right, in one place.

some parts could be extracted and reused in `nvim_buf_set_text`. I need to look over it as it was mainly driven by AI and I still need to use this branch for a while to see if it in practice behaves like I expected a charwise range would behave.
